vocabulary.meaning_en: a place where people buy and sell goods, often outdoors
vocabulary.example: We buy our vegetables at the Saturday market.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an open table or small shop in a market
vocabulary.example: She runs a small fruit stall.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small closed space open on one side
vocabulary.example: Buy your tickets at the ticket booth.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who sells small things in the street or a market; a supplier
vocabulary.example: A street vendor sold us hot corn.

vocabulary.meaning_en: any person or company that sells something
vocabulary.example: The seller wants $5,000 for the car.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something cheap for its value; to discuss a price
vocabulary.note_ar: كفعل مثل negotiate لكنها أقل رسمية
vocabulary.example: We bargained for ten minutes before buying.

vocabulary.meaning_en: costing little money
vocabulary.example: Fruit is cheap at the end of the day.

vocabulary.meaning_en: costing a lot of money
vocabulary.example: Handmade carpets are expensive.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an amount taken off the price
vocabulary.note_ar: dis تعطي معنى الإزالة: count → discount، cover → discover، appear → disappear
vocabulary.example: He gave me a 10% discount.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an agreement to buy or sell; a price that is good
vocabulary.example: That's a good deal for a new phone.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a special price; to say you will give something
vocabulary.example: There's a special offer on rice this week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a time when a shop sells things at lower prices
vocabulary.example: I bought these shoes in the summer sale.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who is shopping
vocabulary.example: The market was full of shoppers.

vocabulary.meaning_en: money in coins and paper
vocabulary.example: Most stalls only take cash.

vocabulary.meaning_en: metal money
vocabulary.example: I have some coins for the parking machine.

vocabulary.meaning_en: paper money
vocabulary.note_ar: note بريطاني (a ten-pound note)، bill أمريكي (a ten-dollar bill)
vocabulary.example: Can you change this fifty-dollar bill?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small bag for money, usually used by women
vocabulary.example: She took a coin out of her purse.

vocabulary.meaning_en: arguing about a price to make it lower
vocabulary.note_ar: فيها إلحاح وجدال، وانطباعها سلبي قليلاً
vocabulary.example: Haggling is normal in this market.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to discuss something to reach an agreement
vocabulary.note_ar: أرقى وأعم من haggle: سعر، موعد، جودة...
vocabulary.example: They negotiated a new contract.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who negotiates
vocabulary.example: She is a skilled negotiator.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a price that is right for both sides
vocabulary.example: Ten dollars is a fair price for this.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something that costs much more than it should
vocabulary.example: Ten dollars for a coffee? That's a rip-off!

vocabulary.meaning_en: how good something is
vocabulary.example: Check the quality before you pay.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small amount to try
vocabulary.example: They gave us free samples of cheese.

vocabulary.meaning_en: used before by someone else
vocabulary.example: I bought a second-hand bike.

vocabulary.meaning_en: made by hand, not by machine
vocabulary.example: She sells handmade soap.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something you buy to remember a place
vocabulary.example: I bought a small souvenir from Cairo.

vocabulary.meaning_en: things made in the area where they are sold
vocabulary.example: I like to support local products.

vocabulary.meaning_en: selling large amounts at lower prices
vocabulary.example: Shops buy their goods at wholesale prices.

vocabulary.meaning_en: full of loud sounds
vocabulary.example: The street is too noisy at night.

vocabulary.meaning_en: having many bright colours
vocabulary.example: The market was colourful and busy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a powder or seed used to add flavour to food
vocabulary.note_ar: spice stall وليس spices stall لأنها هنا تعمل كصفة
vocabulary.example: Cumin is my favourite spice.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a place with houses and shops, smaller than a city
vocabulary.example: I grew up in a small town.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to reach a decision together
vocabulary.example: We agreed on a date for the meeting.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to say yes to what someone asks
vocabulary.example: He agreed to give me a discount.

vocabulary.meaning_en: shown for people to see
vocabulary.example: The new phones are on display in the window.

vocabulary.meaning_en: quickly and without warning
vocabulary.example: Suddenly, the lights went out.

vocabulary.meaning_en: wanting to know about something
vocabulary.note_ar: الاسم curiosity؛ وتختلف عن nosy = حشري
vocabulary.example: The children were curious about the box.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a piece of cloth that covers a window or opening
vocabulary.example: Please close the curtains.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a thick cover used on a bed
vocabulary.example: It's cold; take another blanket.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give out soft light
vocabulary.example: The cat's eyes glowed in the dark.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the story will continue later
vocabulary.example: The episode ended with "To be continued".

fine_lines.title: vendor vs seller
fine_lines.explanation_ar: seller أعم كلمة لأي شخص أو شركة تبيع أي شيء (بيت، سيارة، منتجات). vendor أخص: في السوق والشارع تعني البائع المتجول أو صاحب الكشك (street vendor)، وفي التجارة تعني المورّد الذي يبيع لشركة أخرى. ومنها vending machine لأنها تبيع أشياء صغيرة.

examples.sentence: The seller agreed to lower the price of the house.
They buy fruit from a local street vendor.
Our company changed its software vendor.

fine_lines.title: stall vs booth
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنتان معناهما كشك. stall مفتوح من أكثر من جهة، عادة في الأماكن المفتوحة مثل السوق. booth مغلق من كل الجهات إلا جهة واحدة، مثل كشك التذاكر أو كابينة التصويت. الناس أحياناً يستخدمون booth للكل لأنها تبدو أرقى.

examples.sentence: There's a spice stall near the entrance.
Each voter goes into a voting booth.

fine_lines.title: haggle vs bargain vs negotiate
fine_lines.explanation_ar: haggle مساومة بإلحاح وجدال حول السعر، وانطباعها سلبي قليلاً. bargain تفاوض عادي حول السعر أو الموعد أو الجودة، وهي لغة الحياة اليومية. negotiate نفس معنى bargain لكنها رسمية وتُستخدم في العمل والعقود.

examples.sentence: You can bargain with the sellers here.
The two companies negotiated for weeks.

fine_lines.title: agree on vs agree to
fine_lines.explanation_ar: agree on تعني أن الطرفين وصلا معاً إلى قرار يرضيهما (كلٌّ تنازل قليلاً). agree to تعني أن طرفاً طلب شيئاً والطرف الآخر وافق عليه فقط.

examples.sentence: Finally, they agreed on a fair price.
The vendor agreed to give me a discount.

fine_lines.title: expensive vs rip-off
fine_lines.explanation_ar: expensive وصف محايد: الشيء غالٍ لكن قد يستحق سعره (ساعة فاخرة، سيارة). rip-off تعني أن السعر مبالغ فيه بشكل مستفز واستغلالي، مثل كوب قهوة عادي بعشرة دولارات.

examples.sentence: This watch is expensive, but it's worth it.
Ten dollars for a bottle of water? What a rip-off!

fine_lines.title: offer vs discount vs sale
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الفرق مثل العربية تماماً: offer عرض، discount خصم بنسبة أو مبلغ، sale تنزيلات أو تصفية لفترة.

examples.sentence: The vendor made me a great offer.
The shop isn't having a sale right now.
He'll give me a 10% discount if I buy two items.

expressions.meaning_ar: أنت تساوم بذكاء ولا تتنازل بسهولة
expressions.example: Fine, eight dollars. You drive a hard bargain!
We offer the best price in town.
Be careful, some taxi drivers try to rip you off.
I got a good deal on this laptop.
At first, I didn't like the city.
The story isn't over. To be continued!

grammar.title: Direct and reported (indirect) speech
grammar.explanation_ar: الكلام المباشر (direct speech) ننقل فيه كلام الشخص كما قاله بين علامتي تنصيص. الكلام غير المباشر (indirect / reported speech) نحكي فيه ما فهمناه بأسلوبنا بدون علامات تنصيص. الترجمة حرفية مثل العربية: «قال أحمد إنه كان مشغولاً»، مع الحفاظ على زمن الماضي. كلمة that اختيارية.
examples: Ahmed said, "I am busy." → Ahmed told me (that) he was busy.
Tom said, "I write with my pen." → Tom said (that) he wrote with his pen.
Janet said, "I will clean my room." → Janet said (that) she would clean her room.

grammar.title: Noun used as an adjective
grammar.explanation_ar: عندما يأتي اسم قبل اسم آخر ليصفه يكون في صيغة المفرد لأنه يعمل كصفة. نقول spice stall وليس spices stall، حتى لو كان الكشك يبيع أنواعاً كثيرة.

questions.question: Ten dollars for a small cup of coffee? That's a ___!
After a long discussion, they finally agreed ___ a fair price.
questions.explanation_ar: agree on = توافق الطرفين على قرار مشترك.

questions.question: I asked for a discount, and he agreed ___ give me one.
questions.explanation_ar: agree to = يوافق على طلب شخص آخر.

questions.question: A small closed place where you buy tickets is a ticket ___.
questions.explanation_ar: booth مغلق من كل الجهات إلا واحدة.

questions.question: Which word means "used before by someone else"?
Ahmed said, "I am busy." In reported speech:
choices: Ahmed said he is busy I.
Ahmed said that I was busy.
Ahmed said that he was busy.
questions.explanation_ar: نحوّل I إلى he، ونحافظ على زمن الماضي فتصبح was.

questions.question: In American English, paper money is called a:
Which word is the most formal?
questions.explanation_ar: negotiate رسمية، و bargain لغة يومية، و haggle مساومة بإلحاح.

questions.question: The prefix "dis" in "discount" gives the meaning of:
questions.explanation_ar: dis تعطي معنى الإزالة أو العكس: discover، disconnect، disappear.

questions.question: Selling large amounts of goods at lower prices to shops is:
questions.explanation_ar: wholesale = البيع بالجملة، وعكسها retail = التجزئة.
